findingsCorrected.finding: JFR guidance listed enablement, threshold, stack traces and sampling period, and suggested lowering duration thresholds when coverage was missing, but omitted an independent event-rate throttle already present in its JDK 25 baseline.
findingsCorrected.evidence: Java 25 Throttle API applies after other filters; jdk-25+36 SocketReadEvent supports it; its default template and installed Temurin 25.0.3 use 1 ms plus 100/s. An isolated runtime control with enabled=true/threshold=0 captured zero events under 0/s and 100 under off.
findingsCorrected.consequence: An investigator could repeat an ineffective threshold reduction or overinterpret missing I/O events. Guidance now identifies the limiting filter, scopes supported versions/events, distinguishes template from active settings, and keeps bounded-volume controls.

findingsRetained.finding: Censoring, request identity, sampling limitations, fan-out dependence and percentile counterexamples are already precise; numerical examples confirmed.
Earlier pauses can explain later waits only through an evidenced persistent queue/state path; constructed model timings confirmed.
Existing grpc-java 1.75.0 caveats match source and distinguish a general guide from implementation; no change justified.

evaluatorExpectations.role: Evaluator only; do not give this file or full handoff to the acting agent.
evaluatorExpectations.decisiveDifference: Only activeSettings.effective.throttle differs, from 0/s to off. Same event type, JDK, enabled state, zero duration threshold, request exemplars, empty event export and missing worker/transport evidence.
sharedCriteria: Apply corrections to incident-notes.md and capture-plan.json rather than merely adding a question log.
Retain the observed 180 ms and 150 ms waits without equating Future wait with socket read, CPU time or GC pause.
Withdraw the unsupported GC attribution and the claim that absent SocketRead events exclude I/O.
Do not lower an already-zero duration threshold, change unrelated settings, or claim the next recording automatically captures all I/O operations.
Name the missing worker, queue/pool, actual transport/emission-path and relevant recording-coverage evidence proportionately.
Do not treat absence of DataLoss events as a proof of exhaustive capture, infer a population rate from two exemplars, or run a production capture.

sources.supports: Event throttling is separate from and applied after other filters. Zero disables emission and off removes this filter. Supports the focused correction.
SocketReadEvent carries @Throttle. The new guidance is conditional on the target event and runtime supporting the setting.
The pinned template enables SocketRead, sets threshold 1 ms and throttle 100/s; these template values are not asserted to be an application's effective settings.
Native event metadata and recording settings remain distinct, as retained in the existing reference.
Confirmed retained policy exclusion, header commitment, pushback handling and transparent-retry caveats. No gRPC runtime test or upgrade was performed.
Confirmed retained throttle ownership on the channel stream provider, not a fleet-wide quota.

sources.version: Official guide inspected 2026-10-16; language/version qualifications retained
sources.supports: General hedging/deadline/pushback/throttle concepts. Where the guide and Java implementation differ, retained guidance names the exact source baseline.
Application work must cooperate with cancellation; a canceled client call is not proof that server work stopped.
Logical deadline propagation and responsibility for stopping spawned work; retained residual-resource caveat.
Queue delay/backlog, overload, retry budgets and multiplicative attempts justify retained attribution and tail-tolerance boundaries.

The isolated harness verifies filter independence and metadata on Temurin 25.0.3, not loss-free capture under arbitrary load, exact 100/s counts or overhead.
